course_name_original: Grundlagen der mechanischen und thermischen Verfahrenstechnik (M.104.4200)
course_name_en: Fundamentals of Mechanical and Thermal Process Engineering
prerequisites: Successful completion of modules to be completed in the 1st and 2nd semesters according to the study plan

learning_outcomes.text: Students know and can explain the essential fundamentals and relationships in mechanical process engineering (particle characterization, movement of rigid particles, dimensional analysis, flow behavior of bulk solids, adhesive forces, interactions in colloids).

Students master the design and function of the associated apparatus and their dimensioning for the most important industrial applications, i.e., they are able to practically apply the knowledge acquired here.
Students know and can explain the essential fundamentals and relationships in thermal process engineering (characterization of phase equilibria, concept of the theoretical stage).
Students master the design of the associated apparatus and their dimensioning for the most important industrial applications, i.e., they are able to practically apply the knowledge acquired here.
Students master various complementary aspects and areas of process engineering fundamentals (thermal process engineering, mechanical process engineering).
Students are able to apply the acquired knowledge and procedures to these aspects and areas and to solve the corresponding specific problems successfully and quickly.

syllabus_topics: Basic concepts, material cycles, collectives, application areas
Storage state, particle size distribution, measurement methods
Force balance, laminar and turbulent flow around
Dimensions, Buckingham theorem, solution algorithm, dimensionless characteristic numbers
Viscous and inertia-dominated flow through packings
Flow behavior of bulk solids, storage and silos
Size and types of adhesive forces, strength of agglomerates
Dimensioning of distillation and absorption columns
Process representation in the triangular diagram

assessment_methods.method: Written or oral examination (Module final examination)

assessment_rules: The allocation of ECTS credits occurs if the module final examination is passed. In the examination, students should explain the underlying elementary processes for exemplary problems, and select and fundamentally design suitable processes and apparatus.
